s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities
salient_findings: red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
elevated eosinophil count and tryptase level
key_facts: male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL)
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
negative tests for parasitic infections
skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

raw.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities
salient_findings: red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
elevated eosinophil count and tryptase level
key_facts: male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL)
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
negative tests for parasitic infections
skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of skin lesions with nodular infiltration of histiocytes, lymphocytes, and eosinophils, along with hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and elevated vitamin B12, is most consistent with mastocytosis. The presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene in the bone marrow analysis further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: Lack of lipid-laden foam cells and multinucleated giant cells in skin biopsy

rejected.label: Papular xanthoma
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not match papular xanthoma

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Negative S-100 protein and lack of emperipolesis in skin biopsy

rejected.label: Urticaria pigmentosa
rejected.why: Lesions did not have the characteristic urticarial appearance and Darier's sign was not mentioned
